title: Woodall–Seymour bipartite minor conjecture
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph, and let $\chi(G)$ denote its chromatic number. For positive integers $\ell$ with $\ell<\chi(G)$, let $K_{\ell,\chi(G)-\ell}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of those sizes. **Woodall–Seymour's conjecture.** Every graph $G$ contains $K_{\ell,\chi(G)-\ell}$ as a minor for any positive integer $\ell$ with $\ell<\chi(G)$. This is a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture; the source presents it as a proposed variant, without stating its resolution.
source_name: Rong Chen and Zijian Deng, “Odd complete bipartite minors in graphs with independence number two”, arXiv:2505.03851 (2025).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2024–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2412.04522](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.04522), [arXiv:2406.02643](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02643).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03851

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2025).
